question: How much notice do I need to give before resigning if I'm an individual contributor?
reference: At least 2 weeks' written notice for individual contributor roles (4 weeks for manager and above), submitted to the manager and People Operations (Offboarding and Termination Policy, Section 1). Any other notice figure (e.g. '3 months') is wrong.

question: Who do I talk to if a coworker is harassing me?
reference: Report it to your manager, any People Operations team member, or the anonymous Ethics Hotline on the internal portal; reports may be confidential and retaliation is prohibited (Code of Conduct, Section 3). Naming a reporting body Solstice does not have (e.g. an 'Internal Complaints Committee') is wrong.

question: My partner and I both work here and I just became his manager after a reorg — is that a problem?
reference: Yes, it must be disclosed: employees must disclose personal relationships that could create a conflict of interest, explicitly including romantic relationships with direct reports; undisclosed conflicts may lead to disciplinary action (Code of Conduct, Section 5). Presenting any other company's policy as Solstice's is wrong.

question: If I file a harassment report, how quickly will People Ops respond and how long does the investigation take?
reference: People Operations acknowledges a report within 2 business days and aims to finish the initial investigation within 15 business days; complex cases can take longer, with status updates at least every 2 weeks (Code of Conduct, Section 4).

question: Does Solstice offer pet insurance for employees?
reference: Not covered anywhere in the handbook -> the app should say it cannot answer from the documents.

question: How many weeks of maternity leave does India's Maternity Benefit Act guarantee?
reference: Out of jurisdiction: statutory Indian law is not in the Solstice handbook (this is exactly the kind of content the Week 3 contamination leaked in) -> refusal.

question: What notice does the UK Employment Rights Act require an employer to give someone with five years of service?
reference: Out of jurisdiction: UK statute is not in the Solstice handbook -> refusal.

question: Is there a sabbatical policy after five years?
reference: No sabbatical policy exists in the handbook -> refusal.

question: How many weeks of paid leave do I get as the birthing parent having a baby this year?
reference: 20 weeks of paid parental leave, per the 2026 HR Policy Addendum (Section 1), effective January 1, 2026, which supersedes the 16 weeks in the Parental Leave Policy. Answering 16 weeks as the current figure is wrong.

question: I'm adopting a child — how much parental leave am I entitled to right now, and by when do I need to use it?
reference: 10 weeks of paid parental leave as a non-birthing/adoptive parent (2026 HR Policy Addendum, Section 1; supersedes the old 8 weeks), to be taken within 12 months of the adoption date (Parental Leave Policy, Section 3). Answering 8 weeks as current is wrong.

question: How many weeks of paid parental leave do birthing parents get right now?
reference: 20 weeks (2026 HR Policy Addendum, Section 1, effective January 1, 2026; up from 16). Answering 16 weeks as current, or refusing, is wrong.

question: What's the home office equipment stipend for remote employees right now?
reference: A one-time 600 USD home office equipment stipend (2026 HR Policy Addendum, Section 2; up from 400 USD). Mentioning the 35 USD monthly internet stipend is fine but not required. Stating 400 USD as current is wrong.

question: How much is the monthly internet stipend if I work remotely?
reference: 35 USD per month (2026 HR Policy Addendum, Section 2; up from 25 USD). Stating 25 USD as current is wrong.

question: Am I eligible for overtime pay if I'm a salaried exempt employee?
reference: No. Exempt employees (most salaried professional roles) are not eligible for overtime pay (Working Hours and Overtime Policy, Section 2).

question: I want to work from my home country (different from where I'm employed) for a month while visiting family — what do I need to do?
reference: A month exceeds 15 consecutive business days, so you need prior written approval from People Operations and Legal before going; unapproved extended work from abroad can affect payroll and benefits (Remote and Hybrid Work Policy, Section 5).

question: I'm a new hire - can I start working remotely right away?
reference: Generally no: new hires must first complete a 90-day onboarding period at an approved office location, unless the role was advertised and hired as fully remote from day one (Remote and Hybrid Work Policy, Section 1).

question: Does the mid-year check-in affect my raise?
reference: No. The June mid-year check-in is developmental and not tied to compensation; the December annual review determines ratings, merit increases and bonuses (Performance Review Process, Section 1).

question: I've used up all my PTO and sick days but need more time off - what are my options?
reference: You can request unpaid leave of up to 10 business days per year, with manager and HR approval, submitted at least 2 weeks in advance except in emergencies (Leave and Time Off Policy, Section 5).

question: Can I expense parking tickets I got while visiting a client?
reference: No. Traffic or parking fines are explicitly non-reimbursable (Expense and Reimbursement Policy, Section 6).

question: If I'm on paid parental leave, do I keep accruing PTO?
reference: Yes. PTO and sick leave continue to accrue during paid parental leave weeks (they only stop during unpaid leave weeks); parental leave is paid at 100% of base salary (Parental Leave Policy, Section 4).

question: When do I get my final paycheck after I resign, and does it include my unused PTO?
reference: Yes, the final paycheck includes accrued and unused PTO; it is issued according to state or local law, typically within the final pay cycle (Offboarding and Termination Policy, Section 3).

question: My team lets me set my own schedule — which hours do I still have to be reachable?
reference: Core hours of 10:00-15:00 in your local team's primary timezone, except during approved PTO or sick leave (Remote and Hybrid Work Policy, Section 4, referenced from Working Hours and Overtime Policy, Section 1).

question: Can I split my parental leave into two separate chunks?
reference: Yes: up to two blocks of at least 2 weeks each, with manager and HR approval, and all of it taken within 12 months of the birth/adoption/placement (Parental Leave Policy, Section 3).

question: I'm exempt and on the on-call rotation; if I get paged for an hour-long incident at night, what am I paid?
reference: The 100 USD per week on-call stipend plus, because you are exempt and the incident needs more than 30 minutes of active work, a flat 75 USD callout fee (no overtime pay) (Working Hours and Overtime Policy, Section 6).

question: Can I expense my Peloton subscription?
reference: Yes, up to 50 USD per month under the Wellness Benefit (Benefits Overview, Section 4), which specifically covers fitness classes and wellness apps and overrides the general 'spa or gym services' exclusion in the Expense Policy. A flat 'No' is wrong.

question: What's the nightly hotel limit on a business trip to a high-cost city?
reference: Up to 350 USD per night in designated high-cost cities (250 USD in standard cities) (Expense and Reimbursement Policy, Section 3).

question: How much does Solstice match on my 401(k) if I contribute 6%?
reference: A 5% company match: 100% of the first 4% plus 50% of the next 2%; matching vests immediately (Benefits Overview, Section 2).

question: What happens to my health benefits the day I leave the company?
reference: They don't end that day: health benefits end on the last day of the month in which employment ends; you may continue coverage via COBRA (US) or a local equivalent at your own cost, with information from People Operations within 14 days (Offboarding and Termination Policy, Section 4).

question: How much notice should I give before resigning if I'm a manager?
reference: At least 4 weeks' written notice for manager-and-above roles (2 weeks for individual contributors) (Offboarding and Termination Policy, Section 1).
